chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Husayn ibn Ishaq, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fadala ibn Ayoub, from Sa'dan, from Ajlan Abu Salih, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Abu Salih! When you carry a coffin, be as if you are the one being carried, and as if you asked your Lord for return to the world and He granted it, so look at what you would resume.'
He said, 'Then he said: I wonder at a people whose first ones are withheld from their last ones, then the call for departure is made among them while they are playing.'

key_terms.يَلْعَبُونَ: They are playing (engrossed in worldly affairs)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual perspective recommended when carrying a coffin in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises carrying the deceased with the perspective of one who has just died and is being asked to return to the world, prompting reflection on what one would resume doing. He further expresses wonder at those who are delayed in death while engrossed in worldly play, only to be called to depart suddenly. This narration, found in *Al-Kafi*, highlights the Shia emphasis on *mawt* (death) as a mirror for *hayat* (life), urging believers to treat death not as a distant event but as an imminent reality to ensure spiritual readiness.
